claim: For the periodic antiferromagnetic three-qubit \(XXX\) ring studied by Wang, Fu, and Solomon, take \(J>0\), \(T>0\), a uniform field \(B\), and let \(C(T,B)\) be the concurrence of any reduced pair. Put \(q=e^{3J/T}\) and \(q_0=4+3\sqrt2\). The source's exact field condition implies that there is no thermal entanglement for \(q\le q_0\), while for \(q>q_0\) there is one activation threshold \[B_*(T)=\frac{T}{2}\operatorname{arcosh}\!\left(\frac{(q+2)^2}{q^2-8q-2}\right)\]with \(C(T,B)>0\) exactly when \(|B|>B_*(T)\); this exact threshold is prior-source content rewritten explicitly. The new low-temperature result is a two-scale structure. First, \[B_*(T)\sim \sqrt6\,T e^{-3J/(2T)}\qquad(T\downarrow0).\]Second, around the zero-temperature saturation field \(B_c=3J/2\), for every fixed \(s\in\mathbb R\), \[\lim_{T\downarrow0}C\!\left(T,\frac{3J}{2}+sT\right)=\frac{2}{3(2+e^{2s})}.\]Consequently, every fixed \(B>3J/2\) has the activated tail \[C(T,B)\sim \frac23 e^{-2(B-3J/2)/T},\]every fixed \(0<|B|<3J/2\) has \(C(T,B)\to1/3\), and at \(|B|=3J/2\) one has \(C(T,B)\to2/9\). Thus the low-temperature field diagram contains an exponentially narrow activation layer near zero field and a distinct \(O(T)\) concurrence-amplitude boundary layer at the saturation transition.

correctness.rationale: The source formulas reduce at \(\Delta=1\) to explicit \(u,v,y,Z\). The activation edge follows by monotonic inversion of the exact sign condition. Expanding that edge at \(q=e^{3J/T}\to\infty\) gives \(\sqrt6\,T e^{-3J/(2T)}\). At \(B=3J/2+sT\), dominant exponentials give \(Z\sim e^{(9J/2T)+s}(e^{2s}+2)\), \(|y|\sim e^{(9J/2T)+s}/2\), and \(\sqrt{uv}=o(|y|)\), proving the profile. A direct \(8\times8\) Hamiltonian replay checks the source formula independently.
